name: Cecile Zhang
bio: Cecile Zhang is a cinematographer, filmmaker, and Ph.D. researcher in Digital Media at the Georgia Institute of Technology, where she works with the Augmented Environments Lab. Before beginning her doctoral studies, she worked internationally as a cinematographer across narrative films, documentaries, commercials, music videos, and experimental media. Her work has been recognized by the ExcelLenz in Cinematography at Cannes Film Festival, the American Society of Cinematographers Rising Stars, and Camerimage Film Festival. Her doctoral research explores feminist cinematographic practice, visual culture, and emerging AI technologies. Her dissertation, Visual Parrhesia: Feminist Cinematographic Practice and the Challenge of the Algorithmic Gaze, examines how filmmaking practices and community-governed data infrastructures can challenge biases embedded in contemporary visual technologies.

name: Colin Freeman
bio: Colin Freeman is Director of Technical Art at Paradowski Creative, where he leads 3D art and pipelines for award-winning immersive experiences: Above Par-adowski, the WebXR Awards' Game of the Year; The Escape Artist, a narrative VR puzzle game played by more than 200,000 people in 168 countries; and Purina Arena Pet Racing, Purina's first Roblox game and a Webby winner. A digital media artist and technologist with nearly three decades spanning animation, programming, illustration, and sculpture, Colin was previously a Digital Media Solution Architect at IBM. His doctoral research at Georgia Tech unites perceptual psychology, art history, and machine learning to study how humans compose images within the frame — building computational tools that analyze cinematic composition at corpus scale. An open-source contributor and educator, he publishes WebXR and 3D tutorials, and in essays like The Visual Language of Reality argues that immersive media demands a visual grammar all its own.

name: Watson Hartsoe
bio: Watson Hartsoe is a research engineer and creative technologist who builds working tools for generative media, filmmaking, and worldbuilding. He is a PhD candidate in Digital Media at Georgia Tech, where he develops systems for a problem now shared across creative and technical fields: machines can produce more images, video, code, and possible worlds than people can meaningfully inspect, organize, or shape. His recent work turns that abundance into usable instruments, including browser-based filmmaking systems, networked 3D environments, and compilers that translate formal languages into interactive experiences. He holds an MS in Human-Computer Interaction from Georgia Tech and previously conducted Fulbright fieldwork in Honduras. His work has been recognized by the ITU AI for Good platform, Georgia Tech's AI Competition, CREATE-X, and the Neu Wave AI Film Festival.

name: Soy Jang
bio: Soyoun Jang is a designer, researcher, and PhD candidate in Digital Media at the Georgia Institute of Technology, working at the intersection of media studies and human–computer interaction (HCI). Her work brings historical approaches to speculative design, creating playable speculations that allow people to navigate between multiple pasts, presents, and futures. Prior to Georgia Tech, she earned an MFA in Communication Design from Yonsei University, worked in industry across editorial, brand, and product design, and co-founded Habitus, an independent publishing and social-impact start-up in Seoul.

name: Yuchen Zhao
bio: Yuchen Zhao is a researcher in digital media, XR, human-computer interaction, and human-centered AI. Her doctoral research, including the BioVR project, explored how physiological data can be incorporated into XR to create adaptive interaction mechanisms that respond to users’ physical and emotional states. Her broader interests include digital heritage, new media storytelling, and interactive experience design. She is currently a Postdoctoral Associate at the Yale School of Nursing, where her work focuses on AI-enabled digital health interventions.

name: Daniel Phelps
bio: Daniel Phelps is a media artist, designer, and educator whose work connects large-scale making, spatial storytelling, and advanced technology into a single practice. His research and creative work have been sponsored by NASA, the Oak Ridge National Labs, the Create-X program, the Wagner Foundation, and the PSC/CUNY Research Foundation. He holds a Ph.D. in Digital Media from Georgia Tech and has led academic programs spanning robotics, XR, and media production across more than 20 years of teaching. He currently serves as faculty for the School of Literature, Media, and Communication at the Georgia Institute of Technology.

name: Patrick Fiorilli
bio: Patrick Fiorilli is a writer, critic, and scholar of video games, literature, and media. His work is featured in scholarly journals like Game Studies and Angelaki, as well as in popular venues like the Los Angeles Review of Books and Bright Wall/Dark Room. He holds a Ph.D. in Digital Media from the Georgia Institute of Technology and has taught in the Media Arts and Design Program at the University of Chicago and in the Department of Radio/Television/Film at Northwestern University. He cohosts and produces the literature podcast Pynchon Pals, and writes a newsletter called Critical Theorycraft.

name: Joshua A. Fisher
bio: As an Associate Professor at Ball State University, Fisher’s work explores how emerging technologies shape the ways people create, interpret, and participate in the world around them. As a digital humanist and designer, he builds and studies interactive systems with a particular interest in human agency, community storytelling, learning, and how people negotiate meaning with increasingly intelligent and spatial technologies.

name: Rebecca Rouse
bio: Rebecca Rouse is an Associate Professor in Media Arts, Aesthetics, and Narration and co-director of PlayLab in the Division of Game Development at University of Skövde, Sweden. Rouse’s research spans artistic creation, design with XR technologies, media history, and critical pedagogy. Her focus is the development of new forms of storytelling with new technologies in media theater, games, and interactive narrative. Rouse is the Executive Editor of the ICIDS Book series Interactive Storytelling Art (Play Story Press), a member of the Editorial Board for the journals Digital Creativity, JIB: Journal of Interactive Books, and JINR: Journal of Interactive Narrative Research. Rouse is a co-founder of PlayLab, an interdisciplinary research and performance platform for innovating at the nexus of games, games technology, and the performing arts.

name: Geoffrey Thomas
bio: I create interactive, multimedia experiences that entertain, inform, and engage. I've done this as a designer, artist, curator, teacher, and manager. My work moves across mediums, combining painting, drawing, photography, music, animation, filmmaking, electronics, digital media, and code.
